name: Rogue Drone Patrol
desc: A malfunctioning patrol drone has been circling the scrapyard perimeter for weeks. Neighbors are complaining. Time to put Dad's old frame to the test.
flavor: First flight. First fight. Try not to crash.

narrative.speaker: grandpa
briefing: There's a drone that's been circling the scrapyard since the shutdown.
Neighbors are complaining. Your father's frame is operational — barely.
Go deal with it. And try to bring the frame back in one piece.
debriefing: You did it. That frame responded to you. Just like it did for your father.
...That's not a compliment. He was reckless. Always charging ahead, never listening.
Got him kicked off the force. Got him accused of things I still don't believe.
But you're here. And the drone isn't. That's what matters.

notes: THE tutorial mission. First combat ever. Fixed Rogue Drone, easiest enemy. Grandpa narrates. Unlocks the Outskirts patrol for grinding and the next story mission.

name: Scrapyard Scavengers
desc: Scrap Rats have been stealing parts from the outer piles. Grandpa spotted two of them last night. They're getting bolder.
flavor: Rats in the scrapyard. The four-legged kind would be less trouble.

narrative.speaker: grandpa
briefing: Two of those scavenger punks have been hitting the outer piles.
Stole a servo motor last night. That part was worth more than they are.
Show them this scrapyard isn't free pickings.
debriefing: Scavengers dealt with. For now.
Word gets around when someone starts flying a frame out of a junkyard. Not all of it good.
Your father made enemies. People who wanted him quiet. Those people have long memories.
Keep your head down. Fix the frame. Don't attract attention you can't handle.

notes: First multi-enemy fight (2 Scrap Rats). Still easy but teaches the player that numbers matter. Transitions toward the Docks.

name: The Dockyard Dispute
desc: A fired dockworker has parked his rig across the delivery route. He's demanding severance pay from anyone who passes. The deliveries don't stop for one angry man.
flavor: He's got a hydraulic arm and nothing to lose. Handle with care.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: DELIVERY ROUTE BLOCKED — Industrial Dock Sector 7.
A former KZ Industrial employee is demanding payment from all traffic.
His rig is a modified KZ-7M Ironback. Labor-class, heavy modifications.
Local authorities are not responding. This is your problem now.
debriefing_victory: Route cleared. The worker retreated on foot.
His rig sustained heavy damage — several salvageable parts remain.
ALERT: More displaced workers have been spotted in the dock area.
debriefing_defeat: Tactical withdrawal. Frame sustained significant damage.
The delivery route remains blocked. Repairs recommended before retry.
Partial salvage recovered from the engagement zone.

notes: First REAL fight. Rogue Labor in a medium frame is a step up from fodder. System narrator (not Grandpa) signals the world expanding beyond the scrapyard. First medium part drop on firstClear. Dual debriefings (victory/defeat) for fail-forward.

name: Unwelcome Visitors
desc: Raiders spotted near the scrapyard perimeter. They're not scavenging — they're scouting. If they come back with friends, it won't be a social call.
flavor: The painted skulls on their frames are meant to intimidate. It's working.

narrative.speaker: grandpa
briefing: Saw them last night. Two frames, painted skulls, circling the fence.
They weren't scavenging. They were measuring.
Your father had trouble with their kind too. Deal with the scout before the pack arrives.
debriefing: The scout won't be reporting back.
But they know we're here now. They know what we have.
We need to be smarter. Investigate who sent them.

notes: Defense mission — they come to YOU. Introduces the idea that the scrapyard is a target. Grandpa's debriefing seeds the investigation arc. Scrapyard Raider with weakest_part targeting teaches the player that enemies have different behaviors.

name: Arena Registration
desc: The underground arena is always looking for fresh blood. Registration costs nothing — except whatever happens in the ring.
flavor: The announcer butchers your name. The crowd doesn't care. They're here for the carnage.

narrative.speaker: npc_arena_master
briefing: Fresh meat! Love it. Haven't had new blood in weeks.
Rules are simple: you fight, crowd cheers, winner walks out.
Loser walks out too — we're not animals. Just... enthusiasts.
Your first fight is a qualifier. Win and you're in the circuit.
debriefing: Not bad! Not bad at all! The crowd liked you.
You're in. Amateur circuit — don't let it go to your head.
Come back when you want to fight again. The ring is always open.

notes: Introduces the arena. New speaker (npc_arena_master) with comedic tone contrasts Grandpa's seriousness. No scrap reward — arena pays in glory and creds. Opens both the Amateur arena patrol AND the Corporate Warning story mission.

name: Corporate Warning
desc: An Aegis-Tac security patrol has entered the scrapyard perimeter. They're not attacking — yet. They want to talk. On their terms.
flavor: They follow procedure. The procedure says 'assess threat level.' You are the threat.

narrative.speaker: npc_aegis_officer
briefing: Attention, unlicensed pilot. This is Aegis-Tac Enforcement.
Your frame's signature is flagged in our system. Hayabusa Engineering — that designation was decommissioned.
It was registered to Officer Kazuo Hayashi, NTPD. Status: discharged, pending criminal prosecution. Current status: missing.
You are piloting a frame associated with an ongoing investigation. Stand down for identification.
...Or don't. Either way, we know where you live.
debriefing_victory: Interesting. You fight like a trained pilot. Where did a scrapyard kid learn that?
Officer Hayashi's file says he modified this frame off the books. Unreported upgrades. Unauthorized components.
That's what they charged him with, you know. Among other things.
You've made an impression. Whether that's good or bad depends on what you do next.
We'll be watching.
debriefing_defeat: Stand down. This encounter is logged.
For the record: the Hayashi frame is outdated and poorly maintained. Piloting skill won't compensate forever.
Your father was a better pilot. And even he couldn't outrun what was coming.
We'll be in touch. Upgrade your equipment. Or don't — it won't matter to us either way.

notes: Phase 3 capstone. First elite enemy. Corp Security with balanced stance and tactical targeting is a REAL fight. Requires skill_combat 2 as soft gate. Introduces the corporate threat arc. Both debriefings advance the story — defeat is NOT a dead end. Dad's different approach seeds future narrative.

name: Beyond the Perimeter
desc: The corporate zones begin where the scrapyard ends. Crossing the perimeter means entering their world — their rules, their patrols, their justice.
flavor: The fence has a sign: 'AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY.' You are not authorized.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: ZONE ALERT: Entering Corporate Perimeter — Sector 12.
Multiple frame signatures detected. Aegis-Tac patrol patterns active.
Recommendation: Upgrade equipment before proceeding.
No backup available. You are on your own.
debriefing: Zone traversal complete. Combat data logged.
Corporate patrol frequencies captured — future encounters in this zone will have predictable patterns.
New patrol routes are now available for repeat engagement.

notes: Phase 4 opener. First pool-based story mission (guaranteeArchetype ensures Corp Security appears, but other enemies may too). Requires Hangar Operational — the player needs a Medium frame to compete here.

name: The Taeyang Contract
desc: Taeyang Forge is moving thermal weapons through the docks. Illegal shipment, corporate cover. Someone's paying good creds to intercept.
flavor: Plasma repeaters in unmarked crates. The thermal signature gives them away from a block away.

narrative.speaker: npc_bazaar_contact
briefing: Taeyang Forge is moving hardware through the docks. Thermal weapons — military grade.
The shipment passes through Sector 9 tonight. One escort, Taeyang security.
Intercept the cargo and the contents are yours. Plus my finder's fee.
Fair warning — Taeyang Enforcers run hot. Literally.
debriefing_victory: The crate is open. Heat blades, plasma repeaters... this is serious hardware.
Taeyang will notice the missing shipment. They always do.
But tonight, you're the one with the weapons. Use them wisely.
debriefing_defeat: They got away with the shipment. But now you know what Taeyang is moving through your neighborhood.
Next time, bring better cooling. Those thermal weapons are no joke.

notes: Introduces Taeyang Enforcers and energy weapon theme. New speaker (npc_bazaar_contact) expands the NPC world. First clear guarantees a Taeyang weapon — the player's gateway to energy builds. Victory/defeat both advance knowledge.

name: Bounty: [PLAYER]
desc: Someone put a price on your head. A professional bounty hunter has tracked you back to the scrapyard. This one doesn't give warnings.
flavor: The bounty board is public. Your name appeared on it three jobs ago.

narrative.speaker: grandpa
briefing: Someone put a price on your head. A real one. Not street-level — this is corporate money.
The bounty hunter is already in the district. Professional. Registered with the Arena circuit.
This isn't random. You've been asking questions about your father. Someone doesn't like that.
Your father asked the same questions. Look what happened to him.
...Go. But come back. I'm too old to bury another Hayashi.
debriefing_victory: The hunter powered down. They'll find easier marks.
But the bounty is still active. Someone out there is paying for your head.
We need to find out who. And why.
debriefing_defeat: You survived. Barely. The hunter took what they needed — combat data, frame signature, patrol patterns.
They'll sell that information. The next one who comes will be better prepared.
Grandpa's voice is quiet: 'This happened to your father too.'

notes: The 'they come to you' mission. Veteran Bounty Hunter is the hardest fight so far — wide loadout, tactical targeting, high stats. Defense mission at the scrapyard. Both outcomes seed Dad's story arc. The bounty mystery becomes a narrative thread.

name: Arena — Ranked Debut
desc: You've earned enough reputation for ranked fights. The professional circuit pays better, hits harder, and the crowd remembers your name.
flavor: The lights are brighter up here. So are the weapons.

narrative.speaker: npc_arena_master
briefing: You're moving up! The professional circuit awaits.
Fair warning — these fighters have sponsors. Real equipment. Real training.
The crowd expects a show. Give them one and the glory is yours.
Lose... well, the crowd expects that too. Less fun, though.
debriefing: Professional-grade performance! The sponsors are watching.
Your name is on the boards now. People are talking.
Keep climbing. The Championship circuit is where legends are made.

notes: Arena escalation. Opens Professional circuit patrol for glory farming.

name: Dad's Last Route
desc: Decrypted navigation logs reveal Dad's final known route — through the Neon Bazaar backstreets. The trail is cold, but not dead.
flavor: The coordinates are years old. The questions are older.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: NAVIGATION LOG RECOVERED from archived NTPD patrol records.
Officer Hayashi's last logged patrol deviated from assigned route by 12.7 km.
Destination: Industrial Sector 7, Grid Reference [REDACTED].
Cross-reference: Phantom Works — dissolved engineering collective. Status: dismantled.
A transponder signal. Faint. Intermittent. Broadcasting on a Phantom Works frequency.
Your father went here. Repeatedly. Off the record. The question is why.
debriefing_victory: SIGNAL SOURCE IDENTIFIED: Phantom Works emergency beacon, vintage model.
Someone activated it recently. The signal wasn't here when your father disappeared — it appeared after.
Someone is waiting. Someone who knew your father's route.
Additional data recovered from the beacon: a partial manifest. Frame components. Research notes. Project designation: HAYABUSA MK.II.
Your father wasn't just a cop. He was building something. And he was building it with people who don't officially exist.
debriefing_defeat: Route compromised. Hostiles prevented full traversal.
Partial data recovered: Dad's frame was last pinged near a Phantom Works signal relay.
The connection between Dad and the Exiles is becoming clearer.

notes: The emotional core of Phase 4. Multi-enemy fight (Raider + Exile Operative). Requires skill_investigation 2 — the player must have been exploring, not just fighting. Reveals Dad's connection to Phantom Works. Both outcomes advance the narrative. The Phantom transponder item seeds Phase 5.

name: Restricted Access
desc: Military territory. Every frame here has authorization to shoot on sight. Yours doesn't have authorization to exist.
flavor: IFF transponder reads: UNKNOWN. In military terms, that means TARGET.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: ZONE ALERT: Entering Kuroda Military Command restricted perimeter.
This area is under martial jurisdiction. Unauthorized frames will be engaged without warning.
Intel suggests Commander Steele oversees this sector. Kuroda Heavy Industries' most decorated field commander.
Cross-reference with recovered data: Steele's name appears in your father's investigation notes. She was copied on the report he filed — the one that was classified and then erased.
She may know what happened to your father's evidence. She may have helped destroy it.
Recommendation: Prepare for maximum resistance.
debriefing_victory: Transponder code transmitted. Response incoming... standby.
SIGNAL RECEIVED: 'We know who you are. We knew your father.'
'If you want answers, follow the signal. Come alone.'
Coordinates locked. Somewhere deep in the restricted zone.
debriefing_defeat: Extraction forced. Military response was overwhelming.
Transponder code partially transmitted before withdrawal.
Faint response detected on encrypted channel: '...knew your father...'
Signal source identified. Retry when better equipped.

notes: Phase 5 opener. Military Patrol at high level is the hardest standard enemy. Requires Massive Hangar (Heavy frame access). The Phantom Works responds to Dad's transponder — the endgame narrative kicks in.

name: The Phantom Signal
desc: A Phantom Works operative is waiting at the coordinates. Friend or foe? Only one way to find out.
flavor: The frame's ID reads NULL. The pilot's ID reads NULL. Everything about this reads NULL.

narrative.speaker: npc_phantom_contact
briefing: So you're his kid. You have his eyes. And his stubbornness, apparently.
Your father was building something for us. Something important.
He disappeared before he could finish. We've been waiting for someone to pick up where he left off.
But first — I need to know you can handle yourself. Consider this a job interview.
debriefing_victory: You'll do. You'll more than do.
Your father's work is hidden beneath your scrapyard. He built a lab there — biometric lock, keyed to your DNA.
Go home. Look under the workshop. And when you find what he left behind...
...come find us again. We have work to do.
debriefing_defeat: Close. Not close enough.
I can see his techniques in your piloting. Raw, but the foundation is there.
Come back when you're ready. The work your father started can't wait forever.
But it can wait for you to be strong enough.

notes: The narrative climax before the final arc. Veteran Exile Operative is brutally hard. New speaker (npc_phantom_contact) who KNEW DAD. Victory reveals the Secret Lab location. Defeat still advances the relationship. The item_dads_lab_key is the game's most important unlock. Now unlocks the Scrapyard Siege — the conspiracy's response to the player contacting Phantom.

name: Scrapyard Siege
desc: They came at night. Corporate strike teams, unmarked frames, no IFF signatures. They came for the scrapyard. They came for what's hidden beneath it.
flavor: The one place that was supposed to be safe.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: ALERT: Multiple unregistered frame signatures approaching the scrapyard perimeter.
No IFF transponders. No faction markings. Corporate-grade equipment on unmarked chassis.
Grandpa is in the workshop. He's not answering comms.
The security perimeter is breached. Explosions near the main gate.
This isn't a raid. This is a surgical strike. They know exactly what they're looking for.
debriefing_victory: The attackers are down. Their frames are slag.
But the workshop is burning.
You find him behind the workbench. He'd dragged it across the floor — a barricade over the hidden panel.
He's sitting against it. His hands are burned. The fire suppressor is empty beside him.
He looks up. His voice is a whisper.
'Under the floor. Your father... he built something. For you. I kept it safe.'
A cough. A breath. He reaches for your hand.
'You were always the best thing in this scrapyard.'
His grip loosens.
Outside, the fires die down. The workshop is half-collapsed. But the floor panel is intact.
He made sure of that.
Ichiro Hayashi. Forty years of building. One final act of protection.
The scrapyard is yours now. All of it.
debriefing_defeat: You're pushed back from the scrapyard. The attackers breach the workshop.
By the time reinforcements arrive — Underground contacts, a Phantom operative — the attackers have retreated.
The workshop is gutted. But Grandpa...
He's behind the workbench. He dragged it over the hidden panel. Burned his hands holding the fire suppressor.
He's alive. Barely.
'Under the floor,' he whispers. 'Don't let them take it.'
He doesn't make it through the night.
The medics say the smoke inhalation was too severe. The burns too deep for a man his age.
He fought for forty years of work. He won.
The floor panel is intact.
Ichiro Hayashi. Builder. Protector. Grandfather.
The scrapyard is yours now.

notes: THE emotional gut punch. Grandpa dies protecting the hidden lab entrance. Win or lose, Grandpa dies — the difference is whether you're there when it happens or arrive too late. No cred/scrap rewards — this isn't about loot. 20 glory = the weight of loss. The victory debriefing is his last words TO you. The defeat debriefing is his last words ABOUT the lab. Both paths converge: the floor panel is intact, Grandpa is gone, the lab awaits. This mission MUST exist before msn_dads_secret can trigger.

name: Arena Championship
desc: The final tier. Broadcast across New Tokyo. Every fight is a statement about who you are and what you've built.
flavor: Fifty thousand people watching. No pressure.

narrative.speaker: npc_arena_master
briefing: This is it. The Championship. Broadcast live across New Tokyo.
Your opponent has sponsors, training facilities, and a custom frame.
You have a scrapyard, a legacy, and nothing left to lose.
Somewhere in the crowd, there's an empty seat with a wrench on it. The Underground's way of remembering.
The crowd is ready. The city is watching. Show them what Hayashi steel can do.
debriefing: CHAMPION! The scrapyard kid did it!
They'll be talking about this fight for years. The sponsors are calling. The factions are calling.
You look at the front row. The empty seat. The wrench.
You won. He would have been proud. He IS proud.
The crowd chants your name. But the only voice you want to hear is silent now.
This one was for him.

notes: The arena capstone. Maximum glory and cred rewards in the game. Now happens AFTER Grandpa's death — the briefing and debriefing reflect his absence. The empty seat with the wrench is his memorial. 'This one was for him' is the emotional close of the arena arc.

name: Dad's Secret
desc: Beneath the workshop floor. Behind a biometric lock. Whatever Dad was building, he built it for you.
flavor: The lock responds to your DNA. He knew you'd come looking.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: The workshop is half-collapsed. Burn marks on every wall.
But the floor panel is intact. The workbench — his barricade — is scorched but unmoved.
You clear the debris. Your hands are shaking.
The biometric scanner reads your palm. A click. The floor splits open.
A staircase descends into clean, white light. The air is sterile. Untouched.
No one has been down here since Dad sealed it.
Grandpa kept this secret for years. He died keeping it safe.
Time to find out what was worth dying for.
debriefing: The lab is intact. Preserved. Waiting.
Blueprints cover the walls — frame schematics, material analyses, structural calculations. Years of work.
Tools arranged with precision. Materials cataloged and sealed. Everything labeled in his handwriting.
And on the central console, a blinking light. A recorded message. Queued. Ready.
You press play.
His voice fills the room.
'I'm sorry I can't be there. But everything I know is here. Everything I built is for you.'
'The Mk.II isn't finished — I ran out of time. The blueprints are complete. The materials are cataloged. You'll need help. Find the people I worked with. They'll know who you are.'
'Finish what I started.'
A pause. A breath.
'And take care of Grandpa.'
The recording ends.
The lab hums. The blueprints wait.
You're alone.

notes: THE narrative climax. No combat — pure story. Difficulty 0, encounter mode 'none'. Now requires msn_scrapyard_siege (Grandpa's death). The briefing explicitly references his sacrifice. Dad's recorded message saying 'Take care of Grandpa' is the most devastating line in the game — he asked for the one thing the player can't do anymore. The reward is the Secret Lab structure and the prototype frame blueprint. 25 glory as recognition of the journey. This is where the story currently ends — expansion continues from here.

name: Scrapyard Outskirts Patrol
desc: Regular sweep of the scrapyard perimeter. Drones and scavengers are always showing up.
flavor: Same route, different rats. At least the scrap is consistent.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: Patrol route: Scrapyard Outskirts. Expect minimal resistance.
debriefing: Patrol complete. Area secured.

notes: The first grinding patrol. Easy, farmable, good scrap. Diminishing returns after 5 clears encourage moving to harder content.

name: Docks Security Run
desc: Sweep the abandoned port facilities. Displaced workers and their rigs are getting more organized.
flavor: The hydraulic arms weren't designed for combat. They work anyway.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: Patrol route: Industrial Docks. Medium resistance expected.
debriefing: Docks patrol complete. Salvage collected.

notes: Phase 3 mid-tier patrol. First patrol with medium-category enemy drops. 10% chance of Corp Security encounter keeps it interesting.

name: Arena Match — Amateur
desc: An unranked arena fight. No stakes, no fame — just practice, creds, and the crowd's attention.
flavor: The crowd is small but loud. Mostly drunk.

narrative.speaker: npc_arena_master
briefing: Next fight! Step into the ring when ready.
debriefing: Another one down! Keep fighting, keep climbing.

notes: Arena patrols have better glory and slower diminishing returns — the arena is DESIGNED for grinding. No scrap (arena rules). No equipment drops (arena fighters keep their gear).

name: Corporate Perimeter Patrol
desc: Routine incursion into corporate territory. Aegis patrols, bounty hunters, and the occasional military unit.
flavor: Every time you cross the perimeter, they update your threat assessment. You're moving up the list.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: Patrol route: Corporate Perimeter. High resistance expected. Equipment check recommended.
debriefing: Perimeter patrol complete. Corporate response logged.

notes: Phase 4 primary farming patrol. 5% Military Patrol chance creates occasional 'wall' encounters that test endgame readiness.

name: Bazaar Backstreet Sweep
desc: The alleys behind the Neon Bazaar. Deals go wrong here. Everyone is armed. Trust no one.
flavor: Three types of people in the backstreets: buyers, sellers, and targets. Don't be the third.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: Entering Neon Bazaar backstreets. Hostile contact probability: high.
debriefing: Backstreet sweep complete. Watch your six on the way out.

notes: Phase 4 high-risk patrol. 10% Exile Operative chance = rare Phantom parts drops. 25% Bounty Hunter means mixed loadouts — no two patrols feel the same.

name: Arena Match — Professional
desc: Ranked arena fights. Real stakes, real sponsors, real pain.
flavor: The lights are brighter up here. So are the weapons.

narrative.speaker: npc_arena_master
briefing: Professional circuit! The crowd knows your name. Don't disappoint them.
debriefing: Another victory for the record books! Sponsors are watching.

notes: Best glory farm in Phase 4. Arena diminishing returns are gentler than combat patrols — the arena WANTS you to keep fighting.

name: Restricted Zone Incursion
desc: Deep into military territory. Every encounter here is life-or-death. The rewards match the risk.
flavor: Authorization status: NONE. Survival probability: CLASSIFIED.

narrative.speaker: system
briefing: RESTRICTED ZONE — Lethal response authorized against all unknowns. Proceed at own risk.
debriefing: Zone extraction complete. Combat data archived. Recommend frame maintenance.

notes: Endgame patrol. 40% Military Patrol + 40% modifier chance means constant danger and variation. Drops ceramite and rare materials. The 'test your best build' zone.

name: Arena Match — Championship
desc: Championship-tier fights. Broadcast live. Every opponent is someone's best.
flavor: Fifty thousand watching live. Millions on stream. No pressure.

narrative.speaker: npc_arena_master
briefing: CHAMPIONSHIP ROUND! The city is watching! Give them a show!
debriefing: The crowd goes WILD! Another championship victory!

notes: Best glory farm in the game (12 per run). 50% modifier chance + full tier range. The endgame arena grind for glory-hungry players.
